One Year with the Cybertruck — A Reflection $TSLA

I love my Cybertruck.

I drive it every day. I’ll drive it into the dirt.
Not because it’s perfect — but because it’s mine.

But let’s be honest: Tesla under-delivered. ❌

Depreciation? Brutal.
Paid $110,000. It’s worth maybe $60,000 now.
Expected it. Accepted it. Still hurts.

Build quality? Mine’s fine. Front motor blew out in the first month. Tesla fixed it. No issues since.
Steer-by-wire? Magical. Driving feels like the future.

The real problems aren’t what’s there. It’s what’s missing. 💯

The range is a fantasy.

Originally promised far more.
In reality, I get ~250-280 miles day to day. .
And that’s babying it — no towing, no hauling, no real “truck” use.
Do truck things and the range becomes a joke.

The price?
What was once promised at ~$40K to $60k became ~$100K.

I paid it. Not a big deal.

Full Self-Driving?

Waited 7–8 months for access. Still not on par with Model 3.

Then, days after I paid $8,000 for FSD, they launched a $100/month plan.

Now giving  free one-year FSD trials to new buyers for “training data.”

Early adopters = free QA testers. With no reward.

Range extender?
Cancelled. Quietly.
So if you wanted to use this truck… as a truck…
Too bad. You’re stuck with ~250 to 300 miles.

⸻

Do I regret it? Not at all.
There’s no other car I’d rather own. 🖤

But make no mistake — Tesla looks after Tesla.
And if you’re an early adopter? Expect to be the guinea pig.

I love the company. I love the mission.
But this isn’t the same Tesla that launched the Model S Plaid. 

This one is bigger. Smarter. Sharper.
And a little colder.

Would I do it again?

Probably.

But with eyes a little more open.

There are no guarantees. No steady paychecks. No praise for effort.

To survive, you have to rewire your brain.
Detach from outcomes.
Think in probabilities, not events.
Your edge plays out over hundreds of trades — not one.

The moment I stopped tying every loss to some imaginary expense — a car payment, a dinner, a vacation — everything changed.
I stopped seeing money as money.
I saw it as data.

And that data was teaching me how to master a system that could compound for decades.

If you’re still obsessed with today’s result, you’re not trading — you’re gambling with emotion.
The real edge is in building something that works across years…
Not minutes.
